Gap classes:
1. $recursiveRef targets escape the rule walk (walk.go:346 records only $ref and $dynamicRef sites).
   - VAL-51, new (P blocker): CompileSchema panics with a nil pointer dereference for {"$recursiveRef":"#/x","x":{"multipleOf":1e9999999}}. It also panics for type or required lists of 21 such literals. The panic happens in Check at stage H and in Build, with no recover, so it crashes every binary.
   - VAL-52, new (C1 blocker): compiling these literals costs 22 to 68 ms each. A 459-byte schema takes 0.42 s and allocates 56 MB; a full 256 KiB document would take minutes.
   - VAL-16, confirmed (V1 blocker): at runtime, const or enum [1e99999] at such a target runs at 30 to 58 ns per charged unit.
2. Integer keywords above int64 wrap.
   - VAL-17 (W major): validity is wrong.
   - VAL-50, new (V2 blocker): lengthUnits reads the wrapped negative maxLength as its -1 'absent' value. The decision pass holds 8.95 MB while 104 B is charged. An 80 KB body under 50 such maxLength keywords passes the scan, and Handle peaks at 146 MB.

   - VAL-30, confirmed (C2 blocker): a 13 KB document takes 0.44 to 0.59 s and allocates 167 to 407 MB.
   - VAL-55, new (C3 blocker): the compiled Schema keeps 20 to 41 MB for that 13 KB document, against doc.go's 16 MB claim.
4. VAL-54, new (C1 blocker): URL resolution runs at every reference. Each reference re-parses the base URL, once in the library and twice in the walk. A valid 200 KB schema with a 100 KB $id and 3,500 $refs compiles in 6.3 s and allocates 3.26 GB.
5. Unproven terms and rules (mutants that survive the whole suite):

   - the exponent term of numberWork (VAL-02, major);

critic.summary:
I checked every library function (309 in the non-test files plus kind/kind.go), every keyword string in objcompiler.go and draft.go, and every Go regexp entry point. Almost all of it maps to existing rows. The exception is format assertion, which can be switched on along library-only routes, and that is a new blocker. I added six rows, CC-01 to CC-06. No repository file was changed.

**Functions.** Every function maps to a row by name or by its cited lines, with three exceptions:
- Six functions are never reached or cost only a constant: RegisterFormat, RegisterContentEncoding, RegisterContentMediaType, Draft.String, joinSubschemas and MetaSchemaMismatchError.Error. They need no rows.
- The format.go validators are covered only by VLU-41 (bounded) and section 4.4, which both say they never run on bodies.
- That claim is wrong on library-only routes. A resource with the format-assertion vocabulary, reached through a $recursiveRef target or a base-mismatch target, has format asserted, and the bundled meta/format-assertion meta-schema is enough to give it that vocabulary. The format 'regex' check then calls WP-51's compile-time regexpCache (schema.go:383-403, a plain map) at request time.
- The consequences are a fatal concurrent-map-write crash under parallel requests (3 of 3 runs), memory that grows with each distinct body string, and uncharged request-time work.

**Keywords.** All keyword, path and URL strings map to sections 2.1 and 2.2, except:
- The format-assertion vocabulary gate (objcompiler.go:443) had no row; CC-01 to CC-04 now cover it.
- The draft-04 'id' keyword and the older-draft $ref sibling handling apply only under older dialects. The inspector's DraftVersion backstop catches those, but only after the library has compiled (CC-05).

**Regexp entry points.**
- syntax.Parse at patternsize.go:105 and :163 and at regexcost.go:289: CR-01 to CR-07, CR-26, CR-27.
- syntax.Parse at patternsize.go:437 (the Unicode escape alone): cited by CR-02. Bounded, since all about 1,700 valid escape texts parse in about 4 ms together and the result is cached per document.
- Simplify and syntax.Compile at regexcost.go:290: CR-07, CR-09, CR-10.
- Prog.StartCond, Inst.MatchRune and unicode.SimpleFold: CR-21.
- regexp.Compile at patternsize.go:108: CR-08, CR-11, CR-12, CR-24, CR-28; the library's own init compile: CMP-29.
- MatchString at patternsize.go:94, work.go:504, states.go:576 and on the meta-schema's own patterns: CR-13 to CR-23, CX-29.
- The only uncovered entry point was the request-time compilePattern call on body strings (CC-01 to CC-03).

**Older drafts.** An older-draft dialect at a library-only position also brings in that draft's meta-schema, which applies uniqueItems to enum, so the existing writeHash panic class reaches enum lists (CC-05). Hash collisions among composite list entries in the meta-check are also quadratic at library-only positions, held by MaxSchemaBytes to roughly 0.3 to 0.5 s (CC-06).

**Proposed class.** A new GC-21, 'format and content keywords are annotations on every route', with three parts:
- the inspector refuses any compiled Format or Content* field;
- the regexp engine is frozen after compile;
- GC-01 and GC-02 close the routes.

Its tests should be deterministic, with no heap sampling. CC-05 and CC-06 go to GC-01 and GC-02.

gapClasses.class: GC-01. $recursiveRef and $recursiveAnchor are not first-class references in WP-51. The walk records reference sites only for $ref and $dynamicRef (walk.go:346), but the library compiles $recursiveRef under 2020-12 (objcompiler.go:56-59, :269). So $recursiveRef targets skip every walk rule, count, check order, additionalItems check and checkRef, and no test mentions $recursiveRef at run time.
gapClasses.fix: Round-9 fix (a): define the library's reference keywords ($ref, $dynamicRef, $recursiveRef) once. Use that list in walk.go (sites at :346, follow, checkRef, w.targets, checkOrder, uncheckedPositions), loadIssues, inspect.go:52 and work.go isReference, and pin it with a test against the library's enqueueRef call sites (objcompiler.go:90, 269, 319). Add a post-compile backstop that refuses any compiled Schema with RecursiveAnchor true. Derive the schema side of run-time number work from the compiled values (ratDigits, uncapped exponents). Document the static enforcement next to the dependencies exception, and correct doc.go:19-21 and fuzz_test.go:56-70. The class-wide backstop (every compiled position must have been walked live; recover into RZ-CFG-005) belongs to GC-02.

gapClasses.class: GC-02. The walk's model of which positions the library compiles, with which base and in which order, is not the library's. follow (walk.go:484-496) walks a pointer target once, in site order, with the referencing resource's base (walk.go:494). The library uses the longest collected pointer-prefix resource (roots.go:216-235, root.go:20-32) and collects the $ids of targets checked apart in pointer order. In the other direction, identifies() and inert follows make live what the library never compiles. So the walk's rules are missing at library-only positions, with two consequences the completeness check found. First, an older-draft $schema there brings in that draft's meta-schema, whose uniqueItems on enum reaches the writeHash nil-Rat panic before the post-compile DraftVersion backstop runs (CC-05). Second, the meta-check compares colliding composite list entries pairwise (CC-06).

GC-03. String bytes times uses at compile. MaxSchemaBytes and MaxSubschemas bound the inputs, but nothing bounds a pointer's or URL's length times the number of times the library or WP-51 builds, hashes, compares or keeps it: per position, per value (schema or not), per reference, per resource and per clone.

GC-04. Non-canonical JSON Pointer array indexes in reference fragments. urlPtr.lookup (util.go:234) and WP-51's lookup (pointer.go:113) use strconv.Atoi, so '00', '+0' and '-0' name new positions. The library meta-checks and compiles them again, escaping metaChecks' repeat bounds and pointer-prefix resource matching.
gapClasses.fix: resolveRef and lookup refuse, before the library runs, any array-index token that is not RFC 6901 canonical ('0' or [1-9][0-9]*), at the reference ('does not resolve'), for $ref, $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef. Key metaCount.checked and walker.seen by decoded value identity. Contract request against 07 req 75. CMP-18 also needs GC-02 and GC-03.

gapClasses.class: GC-05. Integer keyword values above int64. intVal (objcompiler.go:499-505) wraps minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems, minProperties, maxProperties, minContains and maxContains, so validity is wrong. A negative wrap also aliases lengthUnits' -1 'absent' sentinel (working.go:523-533), so the working set goes uncharged.
gapClasses.fix: At the walk, either refuse (RZ-CFG-005; an owner decision, with a contract row beside R-77's number rules) or compile a clamped copy (MaxInt64; Raw and Sum unchanged) for every value of the eight integer keywords above math.MaxInt64. Independently, make lengthUnits and every model field read from the compiled schema keep presence apart from value.

gapClasses.class: GC-06. Regex parser work that the lexical pass does not count. Each pattern is parsed four times, and scanPattern (patternsize.go:269-298) misses three costs: parseNamedClass's search to the end of the expression at every '[:' (CR-01), the (?i) Unicode table expansion before cleanClass (CR-02), and alternation factoring (CR-05). The ASCII fold charge is untested (CR-04), and the per-pattern compile transient is unmeasured (CR-09).

GC-07. Dynamic-scope work per step ignores anchor-name bytes and the decision wrapper's frames. working.go:1079-1081 charges a flat 4 units per scope step, while resolveDynamicAnchor (validator.go:781-791) hashes the whole name at every step and validateRefs compares it at every evaluation. scan also starts frames at 0 (working.go:995), although the wrapper adds three scopes.
gapClasses.fix: Record the longest $dynamicAnchor or $dynamicRef anchor (per state or in workFlags) and charge evals x frames x (scopeUnits + anchorLen/nameHashBytes), plus evals x anchorLen/nameHashBytes for the static compare. Start frames at decideFrames and add them to the root value's cycle-check chain. The alternative, a bound on anchor length, needs a contract request.
gapClasses.tests:
- TestWorkCharges rows with 1-, 8-, 808- and 100,000-byte anchors pinning the per-byte difference, and a BenchmarkWorkModel long-anchor case (VAL-46, REFS-29, CX-05);
- the 'dynamic reference' row restated with the wrapper frames, and a row for a $dynamicRef at the root value (VAL-65).

gapClasses.class: GC-08. Peak-heap test assertions sample garbage. peakHeap (working_test.go:200-223) samples HeapInuse at GOGC 10 against a fixed 1 MiB slack. Shapes that churn garbage fail under load, on both the Go 1.26 floor and go1.27.1, while live memory stays within the charge.
gapClasses.fix: Replace every sampled peak with a deterministic live-heap measurement: an x-probe hook that runs runtime.GC and reads HeapAlloc at the deepest point, as decisionTree does, or TotalAlloc bounds on transient copies. Where no probe reaches, keep the 413 regressions without a peak comparison.
gapClasses.tests:
Rewrite each peakHeap user: TestWorkingSetCoversPeak, TestHandleUnevaluatedBranches, TestHandlePatternFit, TestHandleBacktrackCharge, TestHandleAcceptsLargeBodies, TestHandleBoundsMatchedItems, TestHandleBoundsUnevaluatedMemory, TestHandleBoundsValidationMemory and TestPathStates.
Acceptance: the Go 1.26 floor (GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2) and CGO_ENABLED=0 suites pass with -count=10 in three concurrent processes beside busy loops.

gapClasses.class: GC-09. Compile work from counts times counts, outside any budget or benchmark: resource scans per position and per reference, anchors x dynamic anchors, $dynamicRef edge lists, uncounted dependencies array members, number-heavy documents, declared names in states, and compile-time name matching.
gapClasses.fix: Add count terms to GC-03's compile budget, or prove that each product stays within F6 at its bound: resources x (positions + references); anchors x dynamic anchors x name bytes; the sum of $dynamicRef edge-list lengths; dependencies array members counted as positions; declared name bytes in stateBudget. Put every such shape, the number-heavy documents and compile-time matching at their bounds into analysisCases and the combined worst case, and restate the doc.go figures.

gapClasses.class: GC-10. The raw config.schema is decoded in full before the size bound applies: prepare (schema.go:195-213) decodes without MaxCost and only then checks the canonical size.
gapClasses.fix: Decode with a jsonval MaxCost derived from MaxSchemaBytes, or pre-scan the raw bytes, counting canonical bytes with an early stop.

gapClasses.class: GC-11. Go regexp matcher costs are not derived from the compiled program. The transient is charged at 32 KiB + 64 B per instruction (working.go:81-85). Go instead allocates NFA queues by matchPool bucket plus threads, recurses in add() along InstAlt.Out chains on the goroutine stack, zeroes queues on first use, searches literal prefixes, and keeps matchers in sync.Pool.

GC-12. The compiled Schema keeps more than the stated figures (doc.go:113-121, decision 15): decoded enum and const values and rationals, annotation values, Inst slice capacity and prefix copies, and regexp expression text.

GC-13. The number model approximates where the library parses and hashes. The bound and the charges apply below every possible parse site instead of the library's actual ones (a type list containing number, one-item uniqueItems, shape-mismatched composites). The uniqueItems collider estimate for big decimals is crude, and smallRat and hashColliders are untested for exponent forms (07 req 80, decision 14).

GC-14. Values outside the decoder's data model reach the library through the exported M2 API. Schema.Validate and ValidateWithin accept any Go value: invalid types read as valid (validate.go:86-88), arbitrary json.Number text panics or is accepted, and float64 and int parses go uncharged.
gapClasses.fix: Before any library call, the scan rejects every value outside {map[string]any, []any, string, json.Number, bool, nil} and every json.Number that is not an RFC 8259 literal (the jsonval grammar), returning not ok or an error, with recursion bounded by maxNesting. Update the ValidateWithin documentation.

gapClasses.class: GC-15. The stack charge has no absolute ceiling below the Go runtime's maximum. The path term is relative to 8 x maxRequestBodyBytes, which has no maximum (gateway.go:153-155), and a stack overflow is fatal.
gapClasses.fix: Cap the path (stack) term at an absolute ceiling well below the runtime maximum, independent of the configured limits, and answer 413 above it. Include GC-11's add() depth in the term, state the margin in doc.go, and add a contract note against R-77 and 07 reqs 80 to 82.
gapClasses.tests:
- a TestStackWithinCharge-style child process with debug.SetMaxStack(256 MiB) at the largest admitted path, for $ref, allOf, not, $dynamicRef and dependentSchemas chains at 4,095 evaluations x 64 levels, with a large-alternation pattern at the leaf (VAL-53, CX-12);
- a unit test that the cap applies at a 1 GiB configured limit.

gapClasses.class: GC-16. Walk rules and resolution mirrors are not pinned per keyword, form and route. parsedKeywords, subschemaKeywords, the exact-Draft $schema rule and its inert case, joinURL's opaque fix, and the older-draft forms the library still compiles are hand-written lists whose mutants survive the suite.
gapClasses.fix: Derive each set from the library, black-box: the positions it collects, the keywords numVal and intVal parse plus the meta-schema's numeric keywords, and the $schema values getDraft maps to 2020-12. Then generate one table test: every subschema keyword in every form x every rule payload x every route (root, $ref, $dynamicRef, $recursiveRef, anchor, $id resource, referenced additionalItems, inert) x CompileSchema, Check and Factory.Build, expecting the finding pointer, no panic and no load.

gapClasses.class: GC-17. Work-model terms that no test proves. Mutants that remove numberWork's exponent term, parsesOf's const branch, compareWork's string bytes, sortUnits, the 'every' node parse, queueBound's scan charge or the per-loop list of contains all pass the whole suite. There is no uniqueItems working-set case and no bound-digits term for numeric bounds.
gapClasses.fix: A term inventory: for each term of workWeight, scanWeight, enter, the bodyScan methods and the regex analysis budgets, one exact-unit row (TestWorkCharges, TestWorkingSetCharges, TestQueueBoundBudget) whose expected value moves with the term, mutation-checked, plus a BenchmarkWorkModel case per cost shape. Add a bound-digits term for numeric bounds if the new cases exceed 0.8 ns per unit. Also mutation-check the validate rows that were bounded by reading only (section 4.4).

gapClasses.class: GC-18. Keyword locations are not pinned for every error kind (07 req 81). About 20 kinds go through keywordParts' default branch (validate.go:161-178) with no TestValidateKeywordLocation row, and the intent for minContains' location is not recorded.
gapClasses.fix: One TestValidateKeywordLocation row per error kind the library reports under 2020-12, a meta-test that enumerates the kind package's types so that a new kind fails while unmapped, and the minContains intent recorded in doc.go.
gapClasses.tests:
- rows for contains, minContains with and without non-matching items, maxContains, dependentRequired with key 'a/b' (a~1b), dependentSchemas, unevaluatedProperties false, unevaluatedItems false, items false, prefixItems false, multipleOf, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, enum, pattern, minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems, minProperties, maxProperties, then, else, oneOf matching none, propertyNames false, additionalProperties beside patternProperties, and $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef targets;
- the kind enumeration test.

gapClasses.class: GC-19. Compile diagnostics are not deterministic findings at the right pointer. compileIssues (schema.go:406-423) returns library errors the walk did not pre-empt raw, at '', in map order. The fallbacks format whole error trees, checkApart has no fallback, message() rewrites an operator $id that equals a WP-51 URL, and the 64-level decode limit reads as 'not valid JSON'.
gapClasses.fix:
- The walk pre-empts every class of library compile error at its own pointer, in walk order: an unparseable $id at /.../$id; missing anchors and pointers, duplicates, invalid regexes and unsupported vocabularies through GC-01 and GC-02.
- Any residual library error maps to one deterministic finding at the nearest walked position, built from the first leaf's kindMessage, never by formatting a tree; checkApart gets the same fallback.
- message() quotes operator values verbatim.
- Either decode with the configuration's depth limit, or state the 64-level rule with its own message (contract request, round-9 minor 5).
- A FuzzCompileSchema property: identical issues across compiles, and no raw library message.

gapClasses.class: GC-20. Semantic deviations of the library and Go regexp that are neither documented nor pinned. propertyNames' fresh scope loses the outer dynamic anchors. compilePattern's '(?:)' prefix adds a height level. Recursion at Go's height limit is untested. \p classes follow the toolchain's Unicode version (15.0.0 on the floor, 17.0.0 on go1.27.1). RE2's \s and '.' differ from ECMA-262's.
gapClasses.fix: Document each deviation in doc.go and the operator docs, and pin each with a test. Fix the one WP-51 causes (CR-08): add the one-pass guard without adding height, or refuse at the walk with a clear RE2-limit finding. For propertyNames, document the deviation; refusing a $dynamicRef reachable from propertyNames would need a contract request against 07 req 76.

(1) The inspector refuses with RZ-CFG-005, at the keyword, any compiled Schema with Format set, and, as a backstop, any with ContentEncoding, ContentMediaType or ContentSchema set.
(2) Freeze the regexp engine once compileWalked returns: a later call fails and does not cache, and no compiled Schema keeps a reference to the cache's map.
(3) GC-01 and GC-02 close the routes, so the $schema rule applies at every compiled position.
(4) Restate doc.go:22 and the rows' claims.
Asserting format would need its own charges and an ADR. No contract request is needed: 07 req 75 already makes format and the content keywords annotations.
